sources.name: European Court of Human Rights (HUDOC)
sources.coverage: HUDOC search metadata and public document pages. A browser-like session is tried first; Cloudflare-blocked JSON queries and /eng?i= item URLs are replayed in a headless browser, accepting JSON only when its schema is valid and document pages only after the rendered HTML is free of challenge markers.

sources.name: United Nations documents

sources.name: Max Planck Encyclopedia of Public International Law (MPIL)
sources.expected_product: Max Planck Encyclopedias of International Law [MPIL]
sources.user_agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/155.0.0.0 Safari/537.36
sources.fetch_scope: OPIL entry page text from #mainContent: the citation header (title, date, citation(s), content type, product, module, jurisdiction, subject terms) plus, depending on the product and document, either the editorial core issue(s) alone, the encyclopedia entry body, or the full decision text. Measured 2026-10-14: most sampled ORIL report pages returned 1,333-2,266 characters (headnote only; several carried a sign-in prompt for the rest) while Ongwen Trial Judgment law-icl-2038icc21 returned 381,724 characters. Read text_characters before treating a page as a full report.
sources.coverage: Oxford Public International Law search limited to the MPIL product, which since 2024 merges the MPEPIL and MPEiPro modules. Returns the result window with title, author, module, subject terms and a leading excerpt. MPIL became Subscribe-to-Open, so entry pages are normally readable without a subscription; the returned excerpt is not the entry full text.

sources.coverage: Oxford Reports on International Law through the pc_17 product facet. The anonymous whole-product browse reports about 10,034 rows and command responsibility returns 1,011, but that is a coverage count, not full-text access. Result rows carry the citation header, date, jurisdiction, subject terms and the editorial core issue(s), never the report text. Report pages were readable anonymously in only part of the sample; whole-corpus report text is expected to need an institutional session, for which the oxford_reports manual entry remains.

sources.name: Oxford Reports on International Law
sources.limitation: Manual entry, kept for whole-corpus coverage. The anonymous ORIL search is wired up as the separate oril source; reading report text across the whole product is expected to need an institutional session. This entry issues no request of its own. The earlier note that the platform returns HTTP 403 was a User-Agent artifact; a browser-like User-Agent is served normally.
